carboxymethyl.name: carboxymethyl (-CH2COO-)
carboxymethyl.chemistry: Williamson etherification with sodium monochloroacetate after alkalisation
carboxymethyl.effect: introduces anionic charge; drives water solubility and pH/ionic-strength sensitivity

hydroxyethyl.name: hydroxyethyl (-CH2CH2OH)
hydroxyethyl.effect: disrupts interchain hydrogen bonding; nonionic solubilisation, salt tolerant

hydroxypropyl.name: hydroxypropyl (-CH2CH(OH)CH3)
hydroxypropyl.effect: nonionic; lowers gelation temperature, improves film flexibility

methyl.name: methyl (-CH3)
methyl.effect: hydrophobic; gives thermoreversible gelation in methylcellulose

acetyl.name: acetyl (-COCH3)
acetyl.effect: reduces hydrogen bonding and crystallinity; hydrolytically labile

sulfate.name: sulfate half-ester (-OSO3-)
sulfate.effect: strong polyanion; carrageenan/heparin-like, high charge density at all pH

phosphate.name: phosphate monoester
phosphate.effect: anionic; also crosslinks at higher reagent levels

cationic_chptac.name: 2-hydroxy-3-(trimethylammonio)propyl
cationic_chptac.effect: permanent cationic charge; substantivity to anionic surfaces (hair, cotton, skin)

octenylsuccinate.name: octenylsuccinate (OSA) half-ester
octenylsuccinate.effect: amphiphilic starch; emulsion stabilisation (Pickering-type interfacial anchoring)

succinate.name: succinate half-ester
succinate.effect: anionic; mild charge without the hydrophobe of OSA

cellulose.name: Cellulose
cellulose.summary: Linear beta-(1->4)-D-glucan; the reference insoluble biopolymer.
structural_notes: Every second residue is rotated 180 degrees, so the true repeat is cellobiose, not glucose.
The O3-H...O5' intramolecular hydrogen bond plus interchain O6-H...O3 bonding gives crystalline domains and water insolubility.
Derivatisation (CMC, HEC, HPMC, MC) works by disrupting that hydrogen-bond network.
cellulose.formulation_relevance: Substrate in fabric and hard-surface care; the parent of the cellulose-ether rheology modifiers.

cmc.name: Carboxymethyl cellulose
cmc.summary: Cellulose etherified with carboxymethyl groups, typically DS 0.6-0.95.
structural_notes: Substitution is reactivity-weighted: O2 and O6 are favoured over O3.
DS controls solubility; the distribution of substituents along the chain controls salt tolerance and thixotropy as much as DS does.
Anionic, so it is sensitive to hardness ions and to cationic surfactants.
cmc.formulation_relevance: Anti-redeposition polymer in laundry; viscosity modifier.

hec.name: Hydroxyethyl cellulose
structural_notes: Hydroxyethyl groups can themselves be ethoxylated, so molar substitution (MS) exceeds DS.
Nonionic: tolerant of electrolyte and of cationic actives.
hec.formulation_relevance: Thickener in surfactant systems where CMC would be salted out.

hpmc.name: Hydroxypropyl methylcellulose
structural_notes: Two substituent types at different DS; the PoC exemplar carries one at a time.
Thermoreversible gelation on heating is driven by the methyl groups.

amylose.name: Amylose
amylose.summary: Linear alpha-(1->4)-D-glucan; the helical, retrogradation-prone fraction of starch.
structural_notes: The alpha linkage bends the chain into a left-handed helix with a hydrophobic cavity, which is why amylose complexes iodine and fatty acids.
Same monomer as cellulose; the anomeric configuration alone changes solubility, digestibility and morphology.
amylose.formulation_relevance: Contrast case for teaching structure-property relationships.

amylopectin.name: Amylopectin
amylopectin.summary: alpha-(1->4)-D-glucan with alpha-(1->6) branches roughly every 20-25 residues.
structural_notes: Branch points cluster, giving the alternating crystalline/amorphous lamellae of the starch granule.

starch.name: Starch
starch.summary: Granular mixture of amylose (~25%) and amylopectin (~75%); ratio is botanical-source dependent.
structural_notes: Not a single molecule: model amylose and amylopectin separately and state the ratio.
starch.formulation_relevance: OSA-modified starch is a common biopolymer emulsifier.

osa_starch.name: Octenylsuccinate starch
osa_starch.summary: Starch esterified with octenylsuccinic anhydride at DS ~0.02 to make it amphiphilic.
structural_notes: A DS of 0.02 means one substituent per ~50 glucose units, so an exemplar must be at least DP 50 to show one.

chitin.name: Chitin
structural_notes: Amide groups add a second hydrogen-bond donor set, making chitin even less soluble than cellulose.

chitosan.name: Chitosan
chitosan.summary: Deacetylated chitin: beta-(1->4)-D-glucosamine with residual N-acetyl groups; degree of deacetylation (DDA) typically 70-95%.
structural_notes: Cationic below pH ~6.3 (amine pKa); the only common cationic polysaccharide.
DDA is a compositional parameter of the chain, not a substituent DS: model it as a copolymer of glcn and glcnac.
chitosan.formulation_relevance: Deposition aid and antimicrobial; substantive to anionic surfaces.

dextran.name: Dextran
structural_notes: The 1->6 linkage adds an extra rotatable bond per residue, giving a very flexible, highly soluble chain.

pullulan.name: Pullulan
pullulan.summary: Maltotriose units joined alpha-(1->6): a regular (1->4,1->4,1->6) pattern.
structural_notes: Requires an alternating-linkage builder; the PoC builds the (1->4) backbone only and flags the (1->6) junctions as a gap.

alginate.name: Alginate
alginate.summary: Block copolymer of beta-D-mannuronate (M) and alpha-L-guluronate (G), 1->4 linked.
structural_notes: The PoC template library covers the M block only; alpha-L-guluronate is a curation gap.
Ca2+ binding by G-blocks (the egg-box model) is what makes alginate gel; an M-only exemplar cannot show that.

pectin.name: Pectin
pectin.summary: alpha-(1->4)-D-galacturonan, partly methyl-esterified (degree of esterification, DE).
structural_notes: DE, not DS, is the controlling parameter: high-DE pectins gel with sugar and acid, low-DE pectins gel with calcium.
Rhamnogalacturonan regions and neutral-sugar side chains are not represented in a homogalacturonan exemplar.

hyaluronan.name: Hyaluronan
hyaluronan.summary: Alternating beta-(1->3)-GlcNAc and beta-(1->4)-GlcA disaccharide repeat.
structural_notes: A strictly alternating two-monomer repeat; the PoC builder is homopolymeric, so this is flagged as a gap requiring the alternating-sequence builder.
hyaluronan.formulation_relevance: Humectancy and viscoelasticity in personal care.

carrageenan.name: Carrageenan
carrageenan.summary: Sulfated galactans; kappa/iota/lambda differ in sulfate position and count, and in the 3,6-anhydro bridge.
structural_notes: The 3,6-anhydro-galactose ring of kappa and iota is not in the template library: a Phase 2 curation gap.
Sulfate content per disaccharide is the primary classifier: kappa ~1, iota ~2, lambda ~3.
carrageenan.formulation_relevance: Cation-specific gelation (K+ for kappa, Ca2+ for iota).

guar.name: Guar gum (galactomannan)
guar.summary: beta-(1->4)-D-mannan backbone with single alpha-D-galactose (1->6) side groups, M:G about 2:1.
structural_notes: Galactose substitution prevents mannan crystallisation, which is why guar is water soluble and mannan is not.
Cationic guar (CHPTAC-modified) is the standard deposition polymer in shampoo.

beta_glucan.name: Cereal beta-glucan
beta_glucan.summary: Unbranched glucan with mixed beta-(1->3) and beta-(1->4) linkages.
structural_notes: The (1->3) kinks interrupt the cellulose-like ribbon and are the reason it is water soluble; a pure (1->4) exemplar cannot show this. Mixed-linkage sequences need the alternating-sequence builder.

xanthan.name: Xanthan gum
xanthan.summary: beta-(1->4)-glucan backbone with a charged trisaccharide side chain (Man-GlcA-Man) on every second residue.
structural_notes: The real side chain is a trisaccharide with pyruvate and acetate decorations; the PoC can only place a single-sugar branch, so this is an approximation flagged as a gap.
The helix-coil transition and the resulting weak-gel rheology come from the side-chain packing.

inulin.name: Inulin
inulin.summary: beta-(2->1)-linked fructofuranose with a terminal glucose.
structural_notes: Fructofuranose templates and 2-linked anomeric chemistry are not in the PoC library: a declared Phase 2 gap.
